_note: REACHED LIVE at 1440x900 through the production path: three Insert rows
create three elements, then ⌘A (the `select-all` command, which calls
selection.selectAll()) puts all three in the selection and ProInspector
short-circuits to MultiSelectToolbar. Three, because the board's own
header reads '3 selected' and its note ends '…applies it to all three'.
WHAT THE BOARD WON (changed in code):
header 46 -> 48 (159:124). It was hand-rolled out of padding tokens and
landed 2 short; it now uses `.bdi-ehdr`, the same 48h/x16 rule the
single-selection header uses, which is what 159:124 draws too. The
comment that had blamed Gate 14 for the gap was wrong — the gate counts
a bare 48 in the FILE, and the shared CSS rule already spends it once.
all eight align/distribute boxes 32x8radius -> 28x6radius (159:128..133,
159:136/137). flowbite `size="xs"` ships h-8; `tw:h-7` is the same
twMerge group and beats it. That 4px was also why the ALIGN band
measured 76 against the board's 72 and the DISTRIBUTE row 48 against 44
— both now match without touching either section's padding.
238:1428) and their seam. The board runs them CONTIGUOUSLY out of the
DISTRIBUTE row — its first row opens at y164, exactly 48+72+44 — where
the code drew a 1px rule and 12px of padding above them. `.bdi-row-ctrl`
now carries the board's own 34-tall box (28 control + 3 air each side)
and `.bdi-sec-body` drops the 6px gap that used to stand in for it, so
the rhythm is unchanged and the ROW is now the box the board measures.
the colour control 24 -> 28 tall (`.bdi-fill`), matching the numeric
field beside it and both boards' 28.
the note's line box (159:159), `lineHeight: 1.4` -> 16px.
and the shared chassis under all of it: `.bdi-panel` was a rounded,
shadowed card with a border on four sides, inside a column that already
has a background. Nine boards draw the inspector flush with square
corners and at most a left rule (32:2, 807:8521, 159:123, 301:2080,
301:2287…). Flush now — which also gave the body back the 2px the extra
borders were eating.
THE CONTROL COLUMN, and this is the one worth reading twice. Every
profile board and 159:123 fix the control at left 120, width 160 — right
edge on 280 of a 300 frame — and none of them states a label-column
width at all; the label is a text node at left 16. The label grid was
96px, derived as 120-16-8, which put the control at 121..280 = 159 wide,
because the panel's own left rule spends the first of the 300 pixels.
The pixel has to come out of one of the two columns and it now comes out
of the one no board measures: 95px + 8 gap, control 120..280, 160.
NOT JOINED, and why:
draws the control frame white on a `--color/border` #e5e7eb hairline at
radius 6. The six profile boards — 807:8342, :8412, :8475, :8521, :8567,
:8614, all recorded `verified: driven` in boards.json — draw the same
frame `--flowbite/gray/50` on `--flowbite/gray/100` at radius 4. Six to
one, and the six are the family that owns this control, so that is what
ships and that is where these frames are joined (see the profile
recipes). What the two boards AGREE on — 28 tall, 160 wide — is now true
and is measured on those recipes. The frames were `1px solid
transparent` until this change: no resting edge at all, so the hover
state read as the field appearing.
159:127, the ALIGN label's colour. The board says `--color/ink-muted`.
MEASURED: #6b7280 on the `--bk-bg-subtle` band this board also draws is
4.39:1 at 11px, under the 4.5 floor. `--bk-ink-soft` on the same fill is
6.78:1 and is what ships. Conforming would trade a passing contrast
sweep for a diff row. The label's SIZE and LINE BOX match the board and
are visible in the measurement; only the join is withheld. 159:135
(DISTRIBUTE) is the same style on white, where ink-muted would in fact
pass at 4.83:1 — it keeps ink-soft so the two labels in one panel are
one grey, and is measured unjoined for the same reason.
159:159's HEIGHT (28) and WIDTH (268). 28 is a Figma fixed box around a
single 16px line — no renderer produces it. 268 is the panel's full
content width measured from a 300 frame; the shipped panel spends 1 of
its 300 on the left rule, and the note sits inside the property rows'
own 20px right inset, so it reads 263. Its type and colour are joined
and match.
159:158, the 40-tall block the note sits in. It is the note's Figma
wrapper, not a control; the note itself is the element on screen.
